e.etymology: The West African form of Hawa, the Arabic name of Eve, used in Senegal, Mali and the Gambia. Eve goes back to Hebrew Chavah, linked to the word for life.
As a boys' name, a variant of Ari, from Hebrew ari, lion. For girls it is a short form of names such as Ariana and Ariel.
Latin for twins: the constellation of the twin brothers Castor and Pollux and the third sign of the zodiac.

assoc.t: zodiac sign of the Twins, late May to late June

e.etymology: From Hebrew dayan, a rabbinic judge, known as the surname of Israeli general Moshe Dayan. As a first name it is used mainly in Latin America, especially Cuba and Colombia.
A name used mainly in Latin American families, especially Mexican and Costa Rican, as a form of Hania; its source is not settled.
A modern American name in the pattern of Jamar and Lamar with an initial Z. It also matches the Hebrew verb zamar, to make music or sing praise.
A modern coinage joining Cal-, as in Callie, with the -lyn ending.
From Sanskrit riddhi, growth, prosperity and success. In Hindu tradition Riddhi is personified as a consort of Ganesha, alongside Siddhi.
The English word vale, a valley, from Latin vallis, and a surname for someone who lived in one. It also serves as a short form of Valentina, Valerie and Valerio.
A modern Indian girls' name built on Sanskrit yashas, fame or glory, the same root as the boys' name Yash.
A modern spelling close to Zaki, an Arabic name meaning pure, and Zakai, a Hebrew name meaning innocent.
A respelling of Reina, Spanish for queen, from Latin regina. The spelling borrows the English word reign.
A Latin American spelling of Angelin or Angeline, written the way the soft English g sounds in Spanish. The root is Greek angelos, messenger.
A Swedish surname built on Thor, the Norse thunder god, used as a first name alongside Thor, Thorin and Soren.
An Italian name from fiore, flower, from Latin flos; the Italian cousin of Flora.

assoc.t: Fiora, a duelist in the game League of Legends

e.etymology: A modern American coinage in the pattern of Jayce, Chayce and Brayce.
The English word, from Greek theoria, contemplation or a looking at. It joined the wave of word names such as Story, Journey and Legacy in the 2010s.
A literary coinage: it first appears in an 1840s Swedish novel and spread after Marie Corelli's 1887 bestseller Thelma. It is often linked to Greek thelema, will, but that is a later explanation.
namesakes: Thelma Dickinson (Geena Davis's character in Thelma & Louise)
Thelma Houston (singer, Don't Leave Me This Way)

e.etymology: A spelling of Abby, the pet form of Abigail, from Hebrew Avigayil, my father's joy. The spelling matches the English word abbey.
e.note: Also the ordinary word for a monastery or convent, as in Westminster Abbey and Abbey Road.

e.etymology: From Yiddish Hershl, a pet form of Hersh, deer, a traditional name in Ashkenazi Jewish families. The German spelling is also the surname of astronomer William Herschel, who discovered Uranus.
namesakes: Herschel Walker (football star and Senate candidate)

assoc.t: Herschel Walker, football star and Senate candidate

e.etymology: In the US mostly a spelling of Darren. Daron is also an Armenian name, the Western Armenian form of Taron, a historic region of Armenia.
A spelling of Brittany, the English name of the Breton region of northwest France, from Latin Britannia. It took off as an American girls' name in the 1980s.
A spelling of Rachel, from Hebrew rachel, ewe. In Genesis, Rachel is the beloved wife of Jacob and mother of Joseph and Benjamin.
In the US mostly a spelling of Evan, the Welsh form of John. Evin is also an anglicized form of the Irish saint's name Eimhin, and a Kurdish girls' name from evin, love.
Recorded as a Swahili name meaning gift, related to Arabic hadiya. Its US peak in 1999 followed Sarah McLachlan's hit song Adia.
A modern American name, a spelling of Javion, which extends Javon with the -ion ending.
In the US, a K spelling of Cage, an English surname. Kage is also the Japanese word for shadow, familiar from anime and video games.
A respelling of Natalie, from Latin natale domini, the birthday of the Lord: a name once given to girls born at Christmas.
A modern spelling in the family of Alaina and Elaina with an initial M; close in sound to Melania and Malena.
A modern American coinage blending the Bry- of Bryan and Bryson with the -lan ending of Dylan and Rylan.
A respelling of Madison, an English surname meaning son of Maud, a medieval form of Matilda. It became a girls' name after the 1984 film Splash.
A West African form of Fatima, the name of the Prophet Muhammad's daughter, used in Guinea, Mali and the Gambia. Its 1977 US peak followed the character Fanta in the miniseries Roots.
e.note: Most Americans will think of the soda first.
